🍚 Rice Water Calculator

Enter the amount of rice

How much water does rice need?

The amount of water needed to cook rice depends on the variety of rice and the cooking method. There is no single ratio that works perfectly for every type of rice — the best approach is always to check the packet instructions for the specific variety you are using.

As a general starting point, a ratio of 2 parts water to 1 part rice works well for most white rice varieties cooked by the absorption method. This means that for every gram of rice, you add approximately 2 ml of water.

Absorption vs boiling method

The absorption method uses a measured amount of water that the rice absorbs completely during cooking — this is what this calculator is designed for. The boiling method uses a large pot of water that is drained afterwards, similar to cooking pasta, and does not require precise measurement.

Frequently asked questions

Should I rinse rice before cooking?

Rinsing rice removes excess surface starch, which can make the rice less sticky and more separate. If you rinse, you may need slightly less water as the rice absorbs some during rinsing. Basmati and jasmine rice are commonly rinsed before cooking.

Does soaking rice affect how much water I need?

Yes. Soaking rice before cooking allows it to absorb water in advance, so you may need less water during cooking. Basmati rice is often soaked for 20-30 minutes before cooking, which can reduce the cooking water needed.

Why does my rice come out too wet or too dry?

The ratio is a starting point — altitude, pot size, heat level and whether the lid fits tightly all affect the result. If your rice is consistently too wet, reduce water by 10-15%. If it is too dry or burns at the bottom, add a little more water next time.

How much rice should I cook per person?

As a side dish, around 60-75g of uncooked rice per person is typical. As a main dish, 100-125g per person. Rice roughly doubles in weight when cooked, so 100g of dry rice yields approximately 200g of cooked rice.
